# anywhere in the output. The flasher prints a result line after every block it
# writes — "result: block 3 ok", "result: block 4 ok" — and only the final one
# says whether the decoder accepted the whole image. Reading an early line as
# the verdict reported half-written decoders as flashed.
code_before:
port="$1"
image="$2"
log="$(mktemp -t flash)"
trap 'rm -f "$log"' EXIT

echo "Flashing $image to decoder on $port..."

dcc-flash --port "$port" --image "$image" --verify >"$log" 2>&1 || true

verdict="$(grep -E '^result:' "$log" | head -n 1 | sed 's/^result: *//')"

case "$verdict" in
  "image accepted"*) echo "Decoder flashed." ;;
  *)
    echo "Flash failed: ${verdict:-no result line}" >&2
    cat "$log" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

 * used to be called and the caller has to supply one. The new block goes on the
 * end, like a freshly added one, so the numbers operators know blocks by do not
